summary: Corogon's consuls and merchant fleet: southern trade and the island routes, the tariff quarrel, the Crossing purse and the stranded.

tariff_squeeze.name: Squeezed by Parim's Tariffs
tariff_squeeze.desc: Every cargo that crosses the wide sea pays duty twice, once at the Aenoran pier and again at the gate of Parim. The consuls keep the ledger of what they have paid, and they never lose it.

consular_charter.name: The Consular Charter
consular_charter.desc: The ship-owners and the quays have written one charter between them, and the consuls rule by it. Every voter can read it, and many can recite it.

consulates.name: Consulates Abroad
consulates.desc: Corogon keeps a consul in every harbour of the southern coast and on the isles. They collect news, settle disputes and send word home before the news is stale.

convoy_charters_kept.name: Escort Charters
convoy_charters_kept.desc: Merchant ships sail in company under the protection of armed hulls, paid for by a share of every cargo. The sea is long, but the charters hold it together.

parims_charter_ships.name: Under Parim's Charter
parims_charter_ships.desc: Corogon's ships fly the royal charter in Aenoran waters and pay no second duty. The consuls complain about the first, but they pay it.

crossing_purse.name: The Crossing Purse
crossing_purse.desc: The treasury of Corogon has been poured into the western fleet. Ships are chartered, crews are paid and the quays are empty of goods.

corogon_sea_soldiers.name: Sea Soldiers of Corogon
corogon_sea_soldiers.desc: Quay-hands and deck-crews are drilled to fight when the ship is boarded. They are not many, but they know what a gunwale is for.

island_trade.name: The Island Routes
island_trade.desc: A regular sailing now links the harbours of Corogon with the market of Pollos. Salt-fish goes south, wool goes north and both are cheaper for it.

harbour_election.title: Election at the Harbour
harbour_election.desc: The harbour assembly meets on the quay, and the vote is counted in pebbles. The ship-owners want a consul who will lower the dues, and the quays want one who will raise the wages. Both have many pebbles.

corogon_charter.title: A Charter for Corogon's Ships
corogon_charter.desc: A consul of Corogon stands in the antechamber at Parim, with a charter of the kind granted to friendly merchants. He asks that the ships of Corogon be treated as the ships of a friend, and promises that the consuls will remember the kindness.

corogon_embassy.title: An Embassy from Corogon
corogon_embassy.desc: A consul of Corogon and two clerks have landed at Raerby with a casket of seals. They come to open a regular embassy, to settle disputes between the harbours and to share the news of the western shore.

island_routes.title: The Island Routes
island_routes.desc: The consuls of Corogon propose a regular trade between their quays and the market of Pollos: fish and salt south, wool and iron-ware north. The routes will be marked on both charts, and the dues set at a fair figure.

focuses.name: The Consuls of Corogon
focuses.desc: Corogon is governed by consuls, chosen by the ship-owners and the quays. Sobra Canak speaks for them now, from a tall chair in a hall that smells of tar and spice.

focuses.name: The Harbour Assembly
focuses.desc: The assembly meets on the quay at the turn of the tide. Captains, dockers and chandlers all have a voice, and the loudest is the one nearest the water.

focuses.name: The Counting-Houses
focuses.desc: The counting-houses of Corogon lend to half the West. Ves Doran has run the biggest of them for twenty years, and gives the consuls good advice at a reasonable rate.

focuses.name: Elections at the Harbour
focuses.desc: Every four years the harbour assembly elects its consuls. The ships dress their masts, and the quays throw their caps in the water.

focuses.name: Consul Canak's Embassy
focuses.desc: Sobra Canak sends an embassy to Raerby, where the island captains judge the disputes of the western seas. She wants them as friends, and as witnesses.

focuses.name: The Consular Charter
focuses.desc: The harbour writes its customs into a charter, and the charter into its law. After this, a consul who breaks the dues must answer to the assembly, not the other way round.

focuses.name: Southern Trade
focuses.desc: Corogon's fleets sail south for spice, silk and sugar, and north for wool and iron. The quays are widened to take the new cargo.

focuses.name: The Island Routes
focuses.desc: A route is charted between Corogon and the market of Pollos, with beacons, anchorages and a list of rates. The consuls propose it to Pollos with a good dinner and a better map.

focuses.name: Spice and Salt
focuses.desc: Dried peppers, cloves and rock-salt fill the warehouses in the southern quarter. The consuls take a tenth and sell the rest to the West.

focuses.name: The Market Quays
focuses.desc: Three new quays are built to the north of the old harbour, each with a market hall and a customs-house. The harbour is twice the size, and twice as loud.

focuses.name: Consulates Abroad
focuses.desc: A consul is posted in every large harbour on the southern coast. Each has a small house, a flag and a ledger, and each writes home every week.

focuses.name: The Merchant Fleet
focuses.desc: The yards of Corogon build the broad-beamed merchantmen that carry its goods to every shore of the central sea. New slips are cut, and the old ones are lengthened.

focuses.name: Escort Charters
focuses.desc: Merchantmen sail in company under the guard of armed hulls, and pay a share of the cargo for it. The charters are cut on tablets and hung in the harbour-house.

focuses.name: Sea-Captains of Corogon
focuses.desc: Lio Marren is the best of a generation of captains who learned their trade running the southern coast. The consuls give him a commission and a stern message.

focuses.name: The Long Keels
focuses.desc: Corogon builds its first great hulls for war: long, deep and fitted for ramming. They are expensive, and they are very good.

focuses.name: War Galleys of Corogon
focuses.desc: Galleys with thick sides and high prows are laid down in the northern yards. The captains argue about their names, and the carpenters argue about their cost.

focuses.name: Hulls for Hire
focuses.desc: The Ford Council needs hulls and Corogon has them. The consuls quote a price for each, to be paid in advance, and the council agrees.

focuses.name: Tariffs and the Sea
focuses.desc: Parim's tariffs squeeze Corogon hard, and its consuls know the figure to the last coin. The question is whether to bargain or to remember.

focuses.name: The Merchants' Peace
focuses.desc: The consuls decide that a lower duty is worth more than a longer grudge. They send an offer to Parim: a charter for their ships, in return for a lasting peace.

focuses.name: The Sea Remembers
focuses.desc: Every duty paid and every cargo seized is written on a tablet, and the tablets are carried to the harbour-house. The sea is long, and so is Corogon's memory.

focuses.name: Under Parim's Charter
focuses.desc: The charter arrives under the royal seal, and the ships of Corogon fly it at the masthead. They pay one duty, not two, and the consuls say it is the best bargain of the decade.

focuses.name: Relief from the South Sea
focuses.desc: The West will sail to defend the Middle Lands, and Corogon sends hulls with the relief. The ships carry grain as well as spears.

focuses.name: The Purse of the Crossing
focuses.desc: The consuls open the treasury to the Crossing. Ships are chartered, crews are paid, and the counting-houses are told to lend whatever is needed.

focuses.name: The Corogon Pledge
focuses.desc: The consuls swear on the harbour-stone that Corogon will cross. The oath is witnessed by the captains, and entered in the ledger.

focuses.name: The Harbour Guard
focuses.desc: The quays raise a guard of dockers and chandlers, with staves, hooks and a few good swords. It is not an army, but it holds the pier.

focuses.name: Sea Soldiers of Corogon
focuses.desc: The guard learns to fight on a heaving deck, where a spear is better than a sword and a rope is better than a shield. They practise in the harbour on market days.

focuses.name: Crossbow Decks
focuses.desc: A platform for crossbowmen is built on every merchantman, with a rack of bolts and a screen against the spray. A pirate approaching a Corogon ship is a bad day for the pirate.

focuses.name: The Harbour Host
focuses.desc: The guard, the sea soldiers and the crossbow crews are joined into a single host. It is the first in the history of Corogon.

focuses.name: A Ship for the King Without a House
focuses.desc: Several western courts have made a houseless stranger their war-king. Corogon, which knows ships better than kings, sends him a hull and a wayfinder of the old school.

focuses.name: The Crossing Purse Spent
focuses.desc: The treasury has been poured out on the Crossing, and the counting-houses are empty. Corogon has bought the sea for the West, and now it has to live on credit.

focuses.name: Corogon's Stranded Sea-Soldiers
focuses.desc: Some of Corogon's sea soldiers did not sail home. They hold a quay beyond the sea, and they will follow a banner that promises to bring them back.

focuses.name: Home Ports
focuses.desc: The ships come home to Corogon, one by one. The consuls count them in the harbour, and the quays are loud with welcome.
